claim: The reality-check SHAPE — name an unreported confound, impose a controlled protocol, show that published rankings/effects change — is an established, venue-accepted genre (since ~2017).
use: Assert confidently: N1's SHAPE is PRIOR WORK FOUND. The paper's novelty is NOT the shape; it is the offline-MBO residual + the de-confounding direction (N9).

claim: Standard deep nets / deep ensembles are OVERCONFIDENT far from the training data (they assign low uncertainty to inputs far from the data); GP-style distance-aware variance grows away from the data.
use: Assert confidently for N4's mechanism ingredient. But note the qualifier: DUE shows a GP does NOT automatically inherit variance growth.

claim: Infinite-width neural networks converge to Gaussian processes / the neural tangent kernel regime; finite networks are spectrally biased toward low-frequency (smooth) functions.
use: Assert confidently for N5. This is the theoretical spine of the finite-width objection: the 'jagged ensemble mean' may be a width/capacity artifact, cutting against C-mechanism and for D-taxonomy.

claim: No prior offline-MBO work runs a crossed surrogate-class x optimizer factorial with a variance decomposition; the field has not separated surrogate from optimizer contributions.
independent_sources: offline-model-based-optimization-comprehensive-review (Kim TMLR26 — 'whether observed gains stem from superior surrogate modeling, improved optimization strategies, or mere chance')
use: Assert confidently: N6 = NONE FOUND. This is a NEGATIVE consensus — the survey itself names the gap. Load-bearing for candidates A and D.

claim: Implementation / execution-environment details (codebase choice, GPU nondeterminism, hyperparameter reporting, benchmark determinism) can move deep-RL benchmark results by a magnitude comparable to or larger than the method differences under study.
use: Assert for N8's general phenomenon (PRIOR WORK FOUND, partial). Residual = offline-MBO domain + the specific cross-platform (macOS vs Linux) axis + a stated same-order ratio.
